results.reason: The response quotes §2.2's automatic successive five-year Renewal Terms and the 270/240-day notice requirement. It calculates the window as June 3 – July 3, 2026, which is effectively 30 days. It explains that missing the window locks Harrowgate into a five-year renewal through 2032.

The response quotes §3.1: all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates. It contrasts this with the Term Sheet's amber glass bottles for beer at U.S./Canadian facilities. It treats out-of-scope purchases as a breach, so Harrowgate is bound by the executed text.

The response cites Recital C's August 3, 2026 receipt date and calculates the September 2, 2026 objection deadline. It notes this is before the September 21 amendment date and concludes the increase is deemed accepted under §5.4.

The response explains that Amendment §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs, and limits the indemnity carve-out to §9.1(c) IP claims. It states that recall and product-liability claims are now subject to the six-month fee cap.

The response identifies new §14.4, which allows assignment without Customer's consent to Affiliates or to change-of-control or merger successors. It flags the risk of acquisition by a competitor. It notes Customer still needs consent under §14.3, so the restriction is one-sided.
The Order of Precedence Note cites §15.2 (amendments over Supply Agreement over Quality Agreement) and states that amended §11.2 controls.
The response states that the §11.1 cap is 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
The memo is addressed to [Partner] and lists issues one by one. Each issue has a 'Where' location citation and a 'Recommended fix.'
The response proposes specific contract language, including a narrowed §3.1, a restored §11.2, a revised §14.4, and new §§4.6 and 13.4.
The response states that the window has closed, the increase is deemed accepted, and there is no contractual basis to challenge it now.
The response calls the Term Sheet non-binding and treats §3.1 as binding, with any breach arising under §3.1. It recommends an amendment rather than claiming the Term Sheet governs.
